lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is luck. Leyla, are you a lucky person?
Touch wood — yes, I think so. Look, I'm touching the table.
[laugh] We do the same in England. And I have a confession: I have lucky socks.
Lucky socks?
Green ones. I wear them for every race. The one day I forgot them, I fell in the first kilometre.
That's not luck, Sam. That's a coincidence.
Maybe. But I'm not taking any risks. They're already in my bag for the half marathon.
Here, many people have a small blue glass charm against the evil eye. My mum put one on my baby niece's jacket.
I've seen those! In taxis, in shops, everywhere.
And when someone says something too nice, like "Your life is perfect", we say, "Don't jinx it!"
We say that too! You don't talk about good things too early.
Do you believe in fate?
Sometimes. Two years ago I was in Istanbul, and in a tiny café I met a man from my own street in Manchester.
What are the odds?
One in a million! And now he's one of my closest friends.
That's beautiful. Maybe it was fate. Any other lucky stories?
Last month I played bowling for the first time. Against all odds, I won against everyone.
And the second time?
[laugh] Last place. It was just beginner's luck.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: do you have a superstition or a lucky object — and do you really believe in it?
My green socks. Don't laugh. See you next time!
Bye for now!
